=\displaystyle= 𝔼a1:H∼πstu,θ(⋅∣x)[‖∑h=1HDθ,h(x,a1:h)‖22]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{a_{1:H}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\cdot\mid x)}\!\left[\left\|\sum_{h=1}^{H}D_{\theta,h}(x,a_{1:h})\right\|_{2}^{2}\right]
=\displaystyle= ∑h=1H𝔼a1:H∼πstu,θ(⋅∣x)[∥Dθ,h(x,a1:h)∥22]+2∑1≤h<k≤H𝔼a1:H∼πstu,θ(⋅∣x)[Dθ,h(x,a1:h)⊤Dθ,k(x,a1:k)]⏟=0\displaystyle\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{a_{1:H}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\cdot\mid x)}\!\left[\|D_{\theta,h}(x,a_{1:h})\|_{2}^{2}\right]+2\sum_{1\leq h<k\leq H}\underbrace{\mathbb{E}_{a_{1:H}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\cdot\mid x)}\!\left[D_{\theta,h}(x,a_{1:h})^{\top}D_{\theta,k}(x,a_{1:k})\right]}_{=0}
=\displaystyle= ∑h=1H𝔼a1:h−1∼πstu,θ(⋅∣x)[𝔼ah∼πstu,θ(⋅∣sh)[∥Dθ,h(x,a1:h)∥22|x,a1:h−1]]\displaystyle\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{a_{1:h-1}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\cdot\mid x)}\Bigg[\mathbb{E}_{a_{h}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\cdot\mid s_{h})}\!\left[\|D_{\theta,h}(x,a_{1:h})\|_{2}^{2}\,\middle|\,x,a_{1:h-1}\right]\Bigg]
≤\displaystyle\leq ∑h=1H𝔼a1:h−1∼πstu,θ(⋅∣x)[1]=H.\displaystyle\sum_{h=1}^{H}\mathbb{E}_{a_{1:h-1}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\cdot\mid x)}[1]=H.

We have therefore proved the two score identities

𝔼a1:H∼πstu,θ(⋅∣x)[Sstu,θ(x,a1:H)]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{a_{1:H}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\cdot\mid x)}\!\left[S_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(x,a_{1:H})\right] =0,𝔼a1:H∼πstu,θ(⋅∣x)[∥Sstu,θ(x,a1:H)∥22]\displaystyle=0,\ \mathbb{E}_{a_{1:H}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\cdot\mid x)}\!\left[\|S_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(x,a_{1:H})\|_{2}^{2}\right] ≤H.\displaystyle\leq H. (C.16)

Now, we can bound ∇θCw​(θ)\nabla_{\theta}C_{w}(\theta). Fix ww while differentiating with respect to θ\theta.

∇θCw​(θ)\displaystyle\nabla_{\theta}C_{w}(\theta) =∇θ[λm∑j=1m∑a1:H∈𝒜(x~j)πstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)logπstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)πw(a1:H∣x~j)]\displaystyle=\nabla_{\theta}\Bigg[\frac{\lambda}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\sum_{a_{1:H}\in\mathcal{A}(\widetilde{x}_{j})}\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})\log\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}{\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}\Bigg]
=λm∑j=1m∑a1:H∈𝒜(x~j)∇θ[πstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)logπstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)πw(a1:H∣x~j)].\displaystyle=\frac{\lambda}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\sum_{a_{1:H}\in\mathcal{A}(\widetilde{x}_{j})}\nabla_{\theta}\Bigg[\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})\log\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}{\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}\Bigg].

We now expand the derivative of each summand. First, by direct algebra, for any xx, we have

∇θπstu,θ(a1:H∣x)\displaystyle\nabla_{\theta}\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x) =∇θexp[logπstu,θ(a1:H∣x)]=πstu,θ(a1:H∣x)∇θlogπstu,θ(a1:H∣x)\displaystyle=\nabla_{\theta}\exp\!\left[\log\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x)\right]=\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x)\nabla_{\theta}\log\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x)
=πstu,θ(a1:H∣x)Sstu,θ(x,a1:H).\displaystyle=\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x)S_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(x,a_{1:H}).

Moreover, πw\pi_{w} does not depend on θ\theta, and hence we have

∇θlogπstu,θ(a1:H∣x)πw(a1:H∣x)\displaystyle\nabla_{\theta}\log\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x)}{\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid x)} =∇θlogπstu,θ(a1:H∣x)−∇θlogπw(a1:H∣x)=Sstu,θ(x,a1:H)−0.\displaystyle=\nabla_{\theta}\log\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x)-\nabla_{\theta}\log\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid x)=S_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(x,a_{1:H})-0.

Therefore, by the product rule of differentiation, we have

∇θ[πstu,θ(a1:H∣x)logπstu,θ(a1:H∣x)πw(a1:H∣x)]\displaystyle\nabla_{\theta}\left[\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x)\log\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x)}{\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid x)}\right]
=\displaystyle= [∇θπstu,θ(a1:H∣x)]logπstu,θ(a1:H∣x)πw(a1:H∣x)+πstu,θ(a1:H∣x)∇θlogπstu,θ(a1:H∣x)πw(a1:H∣x)\displaystyle\left[\nabla_{\theta}\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x)\right]\log\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x)}{\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid x)}+\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x)\nabla_{\theta}\log\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x)}{\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid x)}
=\displaystyle= πstu,θ(a1:H∣x)Sstu,θ(x,a1:H)logπstu,θ(a1:H∣x)πw(a1:H∣x)+πstu,θ(a1:H∣x)Sstu,θ(x,a1:H).\displaystyle\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x)S_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(x,a_{1:H})\log\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x)}{\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid x)}+\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x)S_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(x,a_{1:H}).

For the second term, its sum is the score expectation already evaluated in (C.16):

∑a1:H∈𝒜(x)πstu,θ(a1:H∣x)Sstu,θ(x,a1:H)=𝔼a1:H∼πstu,θ(⋅∣x)[Sstu,θ(x,a1:H)]=0.\displaystyle\sum_{a_{1:H}\in\mathcal{A}(x)}\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x)S_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(x,a_{1:H})=\mathbb{E}_{a_{1:H}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\cdot\mid x)}\!\left[S_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(x,a_{1:H})\right]=0.

The first equality is the definition of expectation and the second is the first identity in (C.16), applied to this xx and θ\theta. Substituting both product-rule terms into the definition of CwC_{w}, and then using this zero sum, we obtain

∇θCw​(θ)\displaystyle\nabla_{\theta}C_{w}(\theta) =λm∑j=1m∑a1:H∈𝒜(x~j)πstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)Sstu,θ(x~j,a1:H)×logπstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)πw(a1:H∣x~j)\displaystyle=\frac{\lambda}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\sum_{a_{1:H}\in\mathcal{A}(\widetilde{x}_{j})}\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})S_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\widetilde{x}_{j},a_{1:H})\times\log\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}{\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}
+λm∑j=1m∑a1:H∈𝒜(x~j)πstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)Sstu,θ(x~j,a1:H)⏟=0\displaystyle\ +\frac{\lambda}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\underbrace{\sum_{a_{1:H}\in\mathcal{A}(\widetilde{x}_{j})}\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})S_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\widetilde{x}_{j},a_{1:H})}_{=0}
=λm∑j=1m𝔼a1:H∼πstu,θ(⋅∣x~j)[Sstu,θ(x~j,a1:H)×logπstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)πw(a1:H∣x~j)].\displaystyle=\frac{\lambda}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\mathbb{E}_{a_{1:H}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\cdot\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}\Bigg[S_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\widetilde{x}_{j},a_{1:H})\times\log\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}{\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}\Bigg]. (C.17)

In the last line, we rewrite the finite weighted sum as an expectation.

The quantity we want to control has the exact representation

|Cw​(θ)−Cw​(ϑ)|\displaystyle|C_{w}(\theta)-C_{w}(\vartheta)| =|∫01dd​u​Cw​(ϑ+u⁡(θ−ϑ))​𝑑u|=|∫01∇θCw​(ϑ+u⁡(θ−ϑ))⊤​(θ−ϑ)​𝑑u|.\displaystyle=\left|\int_{0}^{1}\frac{d}{du}C_{w}\bigl(\vartheta+u(\theta-\vartheta)\bigr)\,du\right|=\left|\int_{0}^{1}\nabla_{\theta}C_{w}\bigl(\vartheta+u(\theta-\vartheta)\bigr)^{\top}(\theta-\vartheta)\,du\right|. (C.18)

These identities follow from the fundamental theorem of calculus. We bound the gradient appearing here first and then return to this expression. By the triangle inequality, the pointwise log-ratio bound in Lemma B.4, we have

‖∇θCw​(θ)‖2\displaystyle\|\nabla_{\theta}C_{w}(\theta)\|_{2} =λm∥∑j=1m∑a1:H∈𝒜(x~j)πstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)Sstu,θ(x~j,a1:H)×logπstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)πw(a1:H∣x~j)∥2\displaystyle=\frac{\lambda}{m}\Bigg\|\sum_{j=1}^{m}\sum_{a_{1:H}\in\mathcal{A}(\widetilde{x}_{j})}\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})S_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\widetilde{x}_{j},a_{1:H})\times\log\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}{\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}\Bigg\|_{2}
≤λm∑j=1m𝔼a1:H∼πstu,θ(⋅∣x~j)[∥Sstu,θ(x~j,a1:H)∥2×|logπstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)πw(a1:H∣x~j)|]\displaystyle\leq\frac{\lambda}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\mathbb{E}_{a_{1:H}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\cdot\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}\Bigg[\|S_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\widetilde{x}_{j},a_{1:H})\|_{2}\times\left|\log\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}{\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}\right|\Bigg]
≤4​λ​B​Hm∑j=1m𝔼a1:H∼πstu,θ(⋅∣x~j)[∥Sstu,θ(x~j,a1:H)∥2]\displaystyle\leq\frac{4\lambda BH}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\mathbb{E}_{a_{1:H}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\cdot\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}\!\left[\|S_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\widetilde{x}_{j},a_{1:H})\|_{2}\right]
≤4​λ​B​Hm∑j=1m(𝔼a1:H∼πstu,θ(⋅∣x~j)[∥Sstu,θ(x~j,a1:H)∥22])1/2\displaystyle\leq\frac{4\lambda BH}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\left(\mathbb{E}_{a_{1:H}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\cdot\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}\!\left[\|S_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\widetilde{x}_{j},a_{1:H})\|_{2}^{2}\right]\right)^{1/2}
≤4​λ​B​Hm​∑j=1mH=4​λ​B​H3/2.\displaystyle\leq\frac{4\lambda BH}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\sqrt{H}=4\lambda BH^{3/2}.

In the second inequality, we apply Lemma B.4 and in the last inequality, we apply (C.16).

For u∈[0,1]u\in[0,1], the segment between ϑ\vartheta and θ\theta remains inside the student ball because

‖ϑ+u⁡(θ−ϑ)‖2\displaystyle\|\vartheta+u(\theta-\vartheta)\|_{2} =‖(1−u)​ϑ+u​θ‖2≤(1−u)​‖ϑ‖2+u​‖θ‖2≤(1−u)​B+u​B=B.\displaystyle=\|(1-u)\vartheta+u\theta\|_{2}\leq(1-u)\|\vartheta\|_{2}+u\|\theta\|_{2}\leq(1-u)B+uB=B.

Thus, the gradient bound applies at every point of the segment in (C.18). Return to that representation and we get

|Cw​(θ)−Cw​(ϑ)|\displaystyle|C_{w}(\theta)-C_{w}(\vartheta)| ≤∫01|∇θCw​(ϑ+u⁡(θ−ϑ))⊤​(θ−ϑ)|​𝑑u\displaystyle\leq\int_{0}^{1}\left|\nabla_{\theta}C_{w}\bigl(\vartheta+u(\theta-\vartheta)\bigr)^{\top}(\theta-\vartheta)\right|\,du
≤|θ−ϑ|∫012⁡‖∇θCw​(ϑ+u⁡(θ−ϑ))‖2​𝑑u\displaystyle\leq\|\theta-\vartheta\|_{2}\int_{0}^{1}\left\|\nabla_{\theta}C_{w}\bigl(\vartheta+u(\theta-\vartheta)\bigr)\right\|_{2}\,du
≤‖θ−ϑ‖2​∫014​λ​B​H3/2​du=4​λ​B​H3/2​‖θ−ϑ‖2.\displaystyle\leq\|\theta-\vartheta\|_{2}\int_{0}^{1}4\lambda BH^{3/2}\,du=4\lambda BH^{3/2}\|\theta-\vartheta\|_{2}.

This proves (B.11). To prove (B.12), we start with the difference that must be bounded and expand two costs, we have

Cw​(θ)−Cv​(θ)\displaystyle C_{w}(\theta)-C_{v}(\theta) =λm∑j=1m∑a1:H∈𝒜(x~j)πstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)×[logπstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)πw(a1:H∣x~j)−logπstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)πv(a1:H∣x~j)]\displaystyle=\frac{\lambda}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\sum_{a_{1:H}\in\mathcal{A}(\widetilde{x}_{j})}\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})\times[\log\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}{\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}-\log\frac{\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}{\pi_{v}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})}]
=λm∑j=1m∑a1:H∈𝒜(x~j)πstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)×[−logπw(a1:H∣x~j)+logπv(a1:H∣x~j)]\displaystyle=\frac{\lambda}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\sum_{a_{1:H}\in\mathcal{A}(\widetilde{x}_{j})}\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})\times\Big[-\log\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})+\log\pi_{v}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})\Big]
=λm∑j=1m∑a1:H∈𝒜(x~j)πstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)×[logπv(a1:H∣x~j)−logπw(a1:H∣x~j)].\displaystyle=\frac{\lambda}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\sum_{a_{1:H}\in\mathcal{A}(\widetilde{x}_{j})}\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})\times\left[\log\pi_{v}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})-\log\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})\right]. (C.19)

Thus, it suffices to control the difference of calibration log probabilities. We derive that control from the calibration softmax itself:

log⁡πw​(a∣s)=w⊤​ϕ​(s,a)−log⁡[∑b∈ℬ⁡(s)ew⊤​ϕ​(s,b)],\log\pi_{w}(a\mid s)=w^{\top}\phi(s,a)-\log\!\left[\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}(s)}e^{w^{\top}\phi(s,b)}\right],
∇w​log​πw​(a∣s)=\displaystyle\nabla_{w}\log\pi_{w}(a\mid s)= ϕ⁡(s,a)−∑b∈ℬ⁡(s)ew⊤​ϕ​(s,b)​ϕ​(s,b)∑c∈ℬ⁡(s)ew⊤​ϕ​(s,c)=ϕ⁡(s,a)−∑b∈ℬ⁡(s)ew⊤​ϕ​(s,b)∑c∈ℬ⁡(s)ew⊤​ϕ​(s,c)​ϕ​(s,b)\displaystyle\phi(s,a)-\frac{\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}(s)}e^{w^{\top}\phi(s,b)}\phi(s,b)}{\sum_{c\in\mathcal{B}(s)}e^{w^{\top}\phi(s,c)}}=\phi(s,a)-\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}(s)}\frac{e^{w^{\top}\phi(s,b)}}{\sum_{c\in\mathcal{B}(s)}e^{w^{\top}\phi(s,c)}}\phi(s,b)
=\displaystyle= ϕ⁡(s,a)−∑b∈ℬ⁡(s)πw​(b∣s)​ϕ​(s,b).\displaystyle\phi(s,a)-\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}(s)}\pi_{w}(b\mid s)\phi(s,b).

We bound this derivative by the following:

‖∇w​log​πw​(a∣s)‖2\displaystyle\|\nabla_{w}\log\pi_{w}(a\mid s)\|_{2} =‖ϕ⁡(s,a)−∑b∈ℬ⁡(s)πw​(b∣s)​ϕ​(s,b)‖2≤‖ϕ⁡(s,a)‖2+‖∑b∈ℬ⁡(s)πw​(b∣s)​ϕ​(s,b)‖2\displaystyle=\left\|\phi(s,a)-\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}(s)}\pi_{w}(b\mid s)\phi(s,b)\right\|_{2}\leq\|\phi(s,a)\|_{2}+\left\|\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}(s)}\pi_{w}(b\mid s)\phi(s,b)\right\|_{2}
≤1+∑b∈ℬ⁡(s)πw​(b∣s)​‖ϕ⁡(s,b)‖2≤1+∑b∈ℬ⁡(s)πw​(b∣s)=2.\displaystyle\leq 1+\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}(s)}\pi_{w}(b\mid s)\|\phi(s,b)\|_{2}\leq 1+\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}(s)}\pi_{w}(b\mid s)=2.

Since WW is convex, v+u⁡(w−v)∈Wv+u(w-v)\in W for u∈[0,1]u\in[0,1]. The same one-dimensional integration argument, now displayed for the token log probability, gives

log⁡πw​(a∣s)−log⁡πv​(a∣s)\displaystyle\log\pi_{w}(a\mid s)-\log\pi_{v}(a\mid s) =∫01dd​u​log⁡πv+u⁡(w−v)​(a∣s)​𝑑u\displaystyle=\int_{0}^{1}\frac{d}{du}\log\pi_{v+u(w-v)}(a\mid s)\,du
=∫01∇w​log​πw​(a∣s)|w=v+u⁡(w−v)⊤​(w−v)​du.\displaystyle=\int_{0}^{1}\left.\nabla_{w}\log\pi_{w}(a\mid s)\right|_{w=v+u(w-v)}^{\top}(w-v)\,du.

Consequently, we have

|log⁡πw​(a∣s)−log⁡πv​(a∣s)|\displaystyle|\log\pi_{w}(a\mid s)-\log\pi_{v}(a\mid s)| ≤∫01‖∇w​log​πw​(a∣s)|w=v+u⁡(w−v)‖2​‖w−v‖2​𝑑u\displaystyle\leq\int_{0}^{1}\left\|\left.\nabla_{w}\log\pi_{w}(a\mid s)\right|_{w=v+u(w-v)}\right\|_{2}\|w-v\|_{2}\,du
≤∫012​‖w−v‖2​du=2​‖w−v‖2.\displaystyle\leq\int_{0}^{1}2\|w-v\|_{2}\,du=2\|w-v\|_{2}.

Thus, we have

|logπw(a1:H∣x)−logπv(a1:H∣x)|\displaystyle|\log\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid x)-\log\pi_{v}(a_{1:H}\mid x)| =|∑h=1H[log⁡πw​(ah∣sh)−log⁡πv​(ah∣sh)]|\displaystyle=\left|\sum_{h=1}^{H}\bigl[\log\pi_{w}(a_{h}\mid s_{h})-\log\pi_{v}(a_{h}\mid s_{h})\bigr]\right|
≤∑h=1H|log⁡πw​(ah∣sh)−log⁡πv​(ah∣sh)|\displaystyle\leq\sum_{h=1}^{H}|\log\pi_{w}(a_{h}\mid s_{h})-\log\pi_{v}(a_{h}\mid s_{h})|
≤∑h=1H2​‖w−v‖2=2​H​‖w−v‖2.\displaystyle\leq\sum_{h=1}^{H}2\|w-v\|_{2}=2H\|w-v\|_{2}.

Now, we return to the cost-difference representation (C.19). Plugging the bound derived above back, we obtain,

|Cw​(θ)−Cv​(θ)|\displaystyle|C_{w}(\theta)-C_{v}(\theta)| ≤λm∑j=1m∑a1:H∈𝒜(x~j)πstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)×|logπv(a1:H∣x~j)−logπw(a1:H∣x~j)|\displaystyle\leq\frac{\lambda}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\sum_{a_{1:H}\in\mathcal{A}(\widetilde{x}_{j})}\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})\times|\log\pi_{v}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})-\log\pi_{w}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})|
≤2​λ​H​‖w−v‖2m∑j=1m∑a1:H∈𝒜(x~j)πstu,θ(a1:H∣x~j)\displaystyle\leq\frac{2\lambda H\|w-v\|_{2}}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}\sum_{a_{1:H}\in\mathcal{A}(\widetilde{x}_{j})}\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})
=2​λ​H​‖w−v‖2m​∑j=1m1=2​λ​H​‖w−v‖2.\displaystyle=\frac{2\lambda H\|w-v\|_{2}}{m}\sum_{j=1}^{m}1=2\lambda H\|w-v\|_{2}.

The right-hand side is independent of θ\theta. Taking the supremum over θ∈Θ\theta\in\Theta proves (B.12). ∎

Proof of Lemma B.7.

We first verify analyticity, which will also be used in the two Łojasiewicz arguments below. For each fixed legal state ss and token a∈ℬ⁡(s)a\in\mathcal{B}(s), the softmax expressions are

πstu,θ​(a∣s)\displaystyle\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a\mid s) =eθ⊤​ϕstu​(s,a)∑b∈ℬ⁡(s)eθ⊤​ϕstu​(s,b),\displaystyle=\frac{e^{\theta^{\top}\phi_{\mathrm{stu}}(s,a)}}{\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}(s)}e^{\theta^{\top}\phi_{\mathrm{stu}}(s,b)}},
log⁡πstu,θ​(a∣s)\displaystyle\log\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a\mid s) =θ⊤​ϕstu​(s,a)−log⁡[∑b∈ℬ⁡(s)eθ⊤​ϕstu​(s,b)].\displaystyle=\theta^{\top}\phi_{\mathrm{stu}}(s,a)-\log\!\left[\sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}(s)}e^{\theta^{\top}\phi_{\mathrm{stu}}(s,b)}\right].

The exponentials of these linear functions are analytic, and their finite sum is strictly positive on ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d}. Since reciprocals and logarithms are analytic on (0,∞)(0,\infty), both displayed expressions are analytic. For each fixed feasible answer, the chain rule for trajectory probabilities gives

πstu,θ(a1:H∣x)\displaystyle\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x) =∏h=1Hπstu,θ(ah∣x,a1:h−1),\displaystyle=\prod_{h=1}^{H}\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{h}\mid x,a_{1:h-1}),
logπstu,θ(a1:H∣x)\displaystyle\log\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{1:H}\mid x) =∑h=1Hlogπstu,θ(ah∣x,a1:h−1).\displaystyle=\sum_{h=1}^{H}\log\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(a_{h}\mid x,a_{1:h-1}).

Proof of Lemma B.11.

We will apply the nonnegative form of Lemma A.1 with

K=Θ,f⁡(θ)=Δλ,m​(θ),g⁡(θ)=𝒦λ,m​(θ).K=\Theta,\ f(\theta)=\Delta_{\lambda,m}(\theta),\ g(\theta)=\mathcal{K}_{\lambda,m}(\theta).

Accordingly, we verify that the two functions are nonnegative, that their graphs are subanalytic and compact, and that Δλ,m​(θ)=0\Delta_{\lambda,m}(\theta)=0 implies 𝒦λ,m​(θ)=0\mathcal{K}_{\lambda,m}(\theta)=0. We also establish an upper bound on 𝒦λ,m\mathcal{K}_{\lambda,m} to use in the theorem’s exponent normalization. Their definitions are recalled in the lemma statement.

Nonnegativity. By the optimality of θλ,m†\theta^{\dagger}_{\lambda,m} and the nonnegativity of KL divergence, respectively, we have

Δλ,m​(θ)≥0,𝒦λ,m​(θ)≥0,θ∈Θ.\Delta_{\lambda,m}(\theta)\geq 0,\ \mathcal{K}_{\lambda,m}(\theta)\geq 0,\ \theta\in\Theta.

Analyticity. Lemma B.7 proves analyticity for the average KL against any fixed positive answer laws. Apply that result with Qj=πwλ⋆(⋅∣x~j)Q_{j}=\pi_{w^{\star}_{\lambda}}(\cdot\mid\widetilde{x}_{j}) and with Qj=πstu,θλ,m†(⋅∣x~j)Q_{j}=\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta^{\dagger}_{\lambda,m}}(\cdot\mid\widetilde{x}_{j}), respectively. Thus Cwλ⋆C_{w^{\star}_{\lambda}} and 𝒦λ,m\mathcal{K}_{\lambda,m} are analytic. Subtracting the constant Cwλ⋆​(θλ,m†)C_{w^{\star}_{\lambda}}(\theta^{\dagger}_{\lambda,m}) shows that Δλ,m\Delta_{\lambda,m} is analytic.

Compact subanalytic graphs. For F∈{Δλ,m,𝒦λ,m}F\in\{\Delta_{\lambda,m},\mathcal{K}_{\lambda,m}\}, the restricted graph is

graph(F|Θ)={(θ,u)∈ℝd+1:B2−∥θ∥22≥0,u−F(θ)=0}.\operatorname{graph}(F|_{\Theta})=\{(\theta,u)\in\mathbb{R}^{d+1}:B^{2}-\|\theta\|_{2}^{2}\geq 0,\ u-F(\theta)=0\}.

The defining inequality is polynomial and the equality is analytic by Lemma B.7. Hence the graph is semianalytic, and therefore subanalytic. It is also compact because it is the image of the compact ball Θ\Theta under the continuous map θ↦(θ,F⁡(θ))\theta\mapsto(\theta,F(\theta)).

Zero-set inclusion. If Δλ,m​(θ)=0\Delta_{\lambda,m}(\theta)=0, its definition gives

Cwλ⋆​(θ)=Cwλ⋆​(θλ,m†)=minϑ∈Θ⁡Cwλ⋆​(ϑ).C_{w^{\star}_{\lambda}}(\theta)=C_{w^{\star}_{\lambda}}(\theta^{\dagger}_{\lambda,m})=\min_{\vartheta\in\Theta}C_{w^{\star}_{\lambda}}(\vartheta).

πstu,θ(⋅∣x~j)=πstu,θλ,m†(⋅∣x~j),j=1,…,m.\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta}(\cdot\mid\widetilde{x}_{j})=\pi_{\mathrm{stu},\theta^{\dagger}_{\lambda,m}}(\cdot\mid\widetilde{x}_{j}),\ j=1,\ldots,m.
